text: Henry Nolan’s primary motive is to evoke nostalgia and a sense of belonging in response to a rapidly changing world. This intent is structurally supported by his use of the old mill as a central metaphor for stability and resistance against modernity. By anchoring the thematic structure of his short stories in this symbol of tradition, Nolan reinforces the importance of community and heritage, thereby aligning the narrative framework with his goal of preserving a sense of identity amidst societal shifts.
